paper.title: Quasinormal Ringing of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by a King Dark Matter Halo: Higher-Order WKB Analysis
paper.abstract: We study scalar and electromagnetic perturbations of a Schwarzschild black hole (BH) surrounded by a dark matter halo described by the King density profile. The lapse function can be expressed as $1-2[M+M_{\rm DM}(r)]/r$, where $M_{\rm DM}(r)$ is the halo mass enclosed within radius $r$; thus, the halo affects the geometry through its enclosed-mass function. We compute the quasinormal frequencies using the sixth-order WKB method and its Padé-improved version. Rewriting the lapse function in terms of the inverse hyperbolic sine avoids the severe numerical cancellations that arise when evaluating its high-order derivatives. For the configurations examined, the fundamental frequencies agree with those extracted from time-domain evolution to within $0.2\%$.The halo lowers both the oscillation frequency and the damping rate. The change of the real part is almost entirely accounted for by the halo mass enclosed by the photon sphere, and the additional decrease of the damping rate follows the ratio of the Lyapunov exponent to the angular frequency of the circular null orbit. Since part of the halo lies inside the horizon in this metric, we also place the halo outside the BH by means of an Einstein cluster. The frequencies then decrease by a similar amount, but the real part follows the Schwarzschild value multiplied by the gravitational redshift factor of the halo. A jump in the density at the inner edge of the halo scatters the waves and changes the damping rate by up to about $9\%$. For a continuous density profile, deviations from the redshift relation remain below about $1.5\%$ for $r_{\rm in}=3M$ and below about $0.5\%$ for the cases with $r_{\rm in}\geq4M$. No unstable modes are found within the perturbation sectors and parameter configurations examined.

paper.title: Effects of Short-Range Correlations on Quarkyonic Matter
paper.abstract: In this work, we focus on investigating the impact of the short-range correlations on the properties of quarkyonic matter. These correlations induce the scattering of nucleons to momenta exceeding the Fermi momentum, thereby altering the momentum-space occupation distribution that underlies the quarkyonic framework. In particular, we examine to what extent the emergence of a high-momentum tail, due to the short-range nucleon-nucleon correlations, in the momentum distribution, for momenta exceeding the Fermi momentum, affects the fundamental properties of quarkyonic matter, such as the energy density, pressure, and speed of sound, among others. In fact, at high densities, the behavior of the momentum distribution has been established, both experimentally and theoretically, to follow a characteristic $\sim 1/k^4$ dependence at large momenta. To the best of our knowledge, this effect on quarkyonic matter has not yet been systematically investigated. Moreover, this experimentally confirmed feature of the momentum distribution suggests that heavy-ion collisions may probe quarkyonic matter, underscoring the importance of incorporating short-range correlations into a complete quarkyonic model.

paper.title: Faint and Fast Transients from Double Detonations of Low Mass White Dwarfs
paper.abstract: There is significant evidence that white dwarfs can explode via the double detonation mechanism, whereby an initial detonation in an accreted helium shell triggers a second detonation of the carbon-oxygen core. This scenario has been invoked for white dwarfs near a solar mass to produce Type Ia-like supernovae, but low-mass explosions have been relatively unexplored despite the most common white dwarf being near 0.6 solar masses. We predict faint and fast transients emerging from double detonations of white dwarfs with total masses around 0.6 solar masses and accreted helium shells up to 0.3 solar masses. The models are computed through the moving-mesh nuclear hydrodynamics code Cattails and the Monte Carlo radiation transport code Sedona. A continuum of core-powered and shell-powered transients are produced with no more than 0.03 solar masses of radioactive nickel in the core or shell material, respectively. The light curves are rapid and sub-luminous, peaking near -17 magnitudes within 5 to 10 days. The ejecta is dominated by intermediate mass elements and unburnt core that imprint noticeable features in the spectrum. This is the first parameter survey to investigate double detonations at such low masses, and these systems could produce a historically missed population of supernovae. Our predictive models could help large sky surveys find these events.

paper.title: One Method to Find Them All: Analytic Black Holes beyond Einstein
paper.abstract: Rotating black holes offer powerful probes of gravity, but constructing their geometries beyond vacuum general relativity remains challenging. Here we develop a unified framework for constructing stationary, axisymmetric deformations of Kerr from their tidal curvature and physical sources. As a demonstration, we obtain closed-form solutions for six higher-curvature interactions at leading order in the couplings and for generic subextremal spin, without slow-rotation expansions, numerical fitting, or mode decomposition. The solutions pass stringent checks against the field equations, previous mode-by-mode constructions, and known analytic predictions for horizon quantities. We find that the chirality of the interactions organizes the analytic structure of these solutions, a pattern that likely extends to a large class of purely metric higher-curvature theories. Our framework opens a systematic route to black-hole geometries in beyond-Einstein theories and perturbative astrophysical environments. These geometries provide a foundation for strong-field tests with gravitational waves and other observational channels, such as black-hole images and X-ray spectroscopy, as well as theoretical studies of near-extremal black holes.

paper.title: Gravitational wave signatures of periodic orbits around a Schwarzschild-like black hole
paper.abstract: We investigate how deviations from the Schwarzschild geometry affect the motion of massive test particles and the gravitational radiation associated with their periodic trajectories around a new improved Schwarzschild black hole. Periodic configurations are determined by examining the commensurability of the radial and azimuthal orbital frequencies. For representative trajectories, we numerically reconstruct the particle motion and calculate corresponding gravitational wave polarizations using the symmetric trace-free mass-quadrupole approach. By comparing these signals with their Schwarzschild counterparts, we assess how the modified spacetime geometry is encoded in the radiation. Our analysis shows that the parameters $ξ$ and $γ$ produce modest changes in the orbital configurations and their associated waveforms, providing a means of investigating the dynamical signatures of this BH model.

paper.title: "Helium Enrichment Law": The Relation Between Helium and Metal Enrichment in Stars in FIRE-3 Simulations of Milky Way-mass Galaxies
paper.abstract: Helium abundance is a key input to stellar models that are used to infer accurate ages, masses, and compositions for individually resolved stars in the Milky Way (MW), underpinning Galactic archaeology. Since spectroscopically measuring He abundances is difficult, stellar models often assume a fixed "chemical enrichment law" dY/dZ (the slope linearly relating a star's helium mass fraction Y to its metal mass fraction Z). If incorrect, this assumption can introduce significant systematics in inferring stellar properties. Using the FIRE-3 cosmological baryonic zoom-in simulations, we investigate helium versus metal enrichment in the stars of MW-mass galaxies. Given the nucleosynthetic yields in FIRE-3, overall metal production is dominated by core-collapse supernovae (CCSN) at all progenitor metallicities. He production is dominated by CCSN for progenitor metallicities of Z <= 0.1 Zsun, but by stellar winds for progenitors near Zsun. Our simulations produce a range of dY/dZ slopes slopes with best-fit values of ~0.75-2.1 depending on the age of the stars considered at present day; on average consistent with the range of values from MW observations but with no single "universal" enrichment law. The dY/dZ slope also shows galaxy-to-galaxy variance in our simulations, and to leading order increases over cosmic time within the same galaxy, based on the peculiarities of the formation histories of each MW-mass system. Despite choosing a fixed set of nucleosynthetic yields for stellar feedback processes in FIRE-3, we predict variance in dY/dZ for stars in MW-mass galaxies, and observations of MW stars must be interpreted in this context.

paper.title: Effects of Dust in Electron-Capture Supernovae: Difficulty in Explaining Intermediate Luminosity Red Transients
paper.abstract: The progenitors of intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs) spanning the luminosity gap between novae and supernovae are under debate, and electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) have been proposed as a strong candidate. ECSNe from super asymptotic giant branch (super-AGB) stars have been theoretically predicted to be much brighter than ILRTs, but attenuation by dusty winds of their super-AGB progenitors may ease this tension. Here we construct a semi-analytical framework for calculating the light curves of ECSNe with dust attenuation and re-emission, by combining recent ECSN light curve predictions with a model for dust physics. Even by varying both the wind mass-loss rate and the ECSN model parameters, we find it challenging to simultaneously fit the light curve and color evolution of ILRTs. This poses a potential challenge to the standard models of ECSNe for explaining ILRTs. For explaining ILRTs, we propose either the existence of a population of ECSNe with much lower explosion energies ($\sim$10$^{48}$-$10^{49}$ erg) and dimmer plateaus, or alternative model(s) to ECSNe that realize such low explosion energies.

paper.title: The UKIRT M33 Monitoring Project - VII. A 15-year K-band photometric catalogue of long-period variable stars in the central kiloparsec of M33
paper.abstract: We present a homogenised K-band photometric catalogue for the central ${\approx}12$ arcmin$^2$ (${\approx}0.9$ kpc$^2$) of the Triangulum spiral galaxy M33, combining four independent PSF-based near-infrared datasets obtained with UKIRT between 2003 and 2018. These comprise the 2003-2007 UIST multi-epoch monitoring survey, the 2005 UFTI K-band mosaic (for which we present new PSF photometry), new WFCAM PSF reductions for the four central tiles, and a single K-band epoch from the 2018 UKIRT Hemisphere Survey (UHS DR3). Cross-matching all four catalogues and retaining stars detected in at least two of them yields 847 unique stars comprising 21,085 valid K-band measurements spanning a baseline of 15.11 yr. Photometric homogenisation onto the 2MASS/Vega system via 82 low-scatter calibration stars removes systematic inter-dataset offsets of up to 0.22 mag. Of the 847 monitored stars, 771 (91 per cent) are classified as variable ($σ_{\rm rms} > 0.10$ mag), including 385 high-amplitude variables ($A_K \geq 1.0$ mag): prime Mira-type long-period variable candidates for period determination. Cross-matching with archival Spitzer IRAC photometry yields 156 matched stars, of which 120 satisfy $\langle K\rangle - [3.6] > 0.5$ mag, identifying dust-enshrouded AGB candidates inaccessible to all-sky optical surveys. This catalogue constitutes the most extensive near-infrared photometric baseline assembled for AGB stars in any spiral galaxy beyond the Milky Way, providing the photometric foundation for the period-luminosity analysis and star-formation-history reconstruction in the companion Paper VIII. The full catalogue is available at the Centre de Données astronomiques de Strasbourg (CDS).

paper.title: A self-supervised machine learning approach to identify instrumental systematics in 21cm Cosmology
paper.abstract: The primordial sound waves in the baryon-photon plasma are imprinted on the large-scale galaxy distribution as Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO), serving as a cosmological standard ruler to constrain dark energy and the Hubble parameter. The upcoming 21cm intensity-mapping arrays are designed to map the 21cm emission across large volumes and measure the BAO scale. However, radio interferometers suffer from instrumental systematics that can hinder detection of the cosmological 21cm signal by leaking bright foregrounds into the signal-dominated modes. This work aims to demonstrate that a self-supervised model can predict the instrument systematic state (here, the amplitude of a spectral ripple in the beam width) in interferometric visibilities and potentially disentangle the instrument from the sky without a forward model. Based on the fact that an instrument stays the same as the sky rotates in a drift-scan observation, and that the same sky is observed under different instrument states, we train a convolutional autoencoder to compress the information in the simulated visibilities and separate this information into instrument-only and sky-only latent vectors. The result shows excellent prediction of the unknown instrument systematic for 15 held-out instrument states with $R^2 = 0.9975$ with a linear probe, against $R^2 = -3.55$ for a random-encoder baseline. The instrument-latent carries no detectable sky signal, as measured with a total-power sky proxy, for any held-out test data. The sky-latent vector and instrument-latent vector show partial separation but not complete disentanglement, identifying sky-latent purity as the primary open problem. The results show the ability of the model to recognize the systematic and show a promising path towards an ML-based foreground cleaning pipeline. Full instrument-sky disentanglement constitutes the natural next step.

paper.title: Cosmological Constraints on Interacting Dark Matter with SPT-3G D1
paper.abstract: Models of the dark sector in which the dark matter participates in nontrivial interactions can create detectable signatures in cosmological observables, providing non-terrestrial means of probing the nature of dark matter. In this work, we test dark matter-baryon scattering, dark matter-dark radiation interactions, and dark matter annihilation using measurements of the CMB and BAO. We leverage the latest SPT-3G D1 CMB measurements of the primary anisotropies, alongside the D1 MUSE lensing data, to set up-to-date bounds on these models. From the combination of Planck, ACT DR6, and SPT-3G D1 data, we constrain the velocity-independent dark matter-baryon scattering cross-section to $σ_\mathrm{DM-b} < 4.6\times10^{-26}~\mathrm{cm^2}$, the dark matter-dark radiation momentum transfer rate to $Γ_\mathrm{0,nadm}<5.2\times10^{-8}\,\text{Mpc}^{-1}$, and the effective dark matter annihilation parameter, quantifying the fractional thermally averaged cross-section, to $p_\mathrm{ann}<3.7\times10^{-28}~\mathrm{cm^3/s/GeV}$, all at the 95% confidence level. The improved sensitivity to the first two models is in particular driven by the precision measurements of CMB lensing at small scales provided by SPT-3G D1 MUSE lensing data. For annihilating dark matter, due to the degeneracy of the effect with the optical depth to reionization, we observe a non-trivial relationship between the upper bound on $p_\mathrm{ann}$ and the large-scale polarization information. When combining CMB data with the latest measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), upper bounds on extended model parameters can appear to tighten as the model space attempts to accommodate the known discrepancy between these data. Future CMB and BAO measurements will provide better clarity on reconciling this discrepancy and enhance our ability to test dark matter interactions.

paper.title: A Quiet Night in the Millihertz Sky? LISA Forecasts from LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Populations
paper.abstract: The high-mass black hole population inferred from ground-based observations can substantially affect the number of binaries detectable by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). We use population constraints based on data from the latest LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-5.0), as well as constraints from the O3 search for intermediate-mass black hole binaries, to forecast the number and masses of binary black holes detectable by LISA. Using the released GWTC-5.0 population posterior, we obtain $6.6^{+5.5}_{-2.2}$ expected detections with signal-to-noise ratio $>8$ in 4 years (median and $90\%$ credible interval). The alternative population models we consider use a broken power law with two or three Gaussian peaks for either the primary-mass distribution or a common mass distribution for both black holes. For the three-peak model with the common mass distribution, extrapolating from $300$ to $1000M_\odot$ roughly doubles the median expected number of LISA detections to $\sim14$. The upper end of its $90\%$ credible interval rises from tens to thousands of expected detections, although approximations may limit the reliability of the most extreme counts. For the reference GWTC-5.0 population, $39^{+22}_{-11}\%$ of the binaries detectable by LISA merge during the mission or within $10$ years after its end and are potential multiband sources. Essentially all of these mergers would be detectable by a reference Cosmic Explorer configuration if it is operating at merger. Ground-based measurements of the high-mass population can therefore inform both LISA forecasts and the prospects for observing the same binaries through inspiral and merger.

paper.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
paper.abstract: It is commonly assumed that the mass of dark matter particles cannot be determined from their gravitational effects when dark matter behaves as collisionless matter. Here we show that extreme-mass-ratio inspirals observable by millihertz gravitational-wave observatories such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could measure the mass of ultralight dark matter particles in sufficiently dense dark matter spikes. The separation of scales between the two black holes allows ultralight dark matter to form a collisionless density spike around the massive primary while retaining wave effects in its interaction with the stellar-mass companion. We incorporate wave-dependent accretion and dynamical friction into relativistic inspiral waveforms and jointly infer the dark matter particle mass, spike normalisation and binary parameters from simulated LISA signals. For massive black holes at the low-mass end of the LISA population ($M\sim 10^5 M_\odot$), our forecasts show that particle masses spanning $10^{-14}-10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$ could be measured to within an order of magnitude.

paper.title: Measuring the magnetization profiles of galaxy groups and clusters
paper.abstract: Magnetic fields are vital in determining the physical conditions of baryons in massive halos. They are, however, notoriously difficult to observe. This impacts problems from our understanding of galaxy formation, to the observed deficit in the amplitude of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) power spectrum that affects cosmological inferences. Although Faraday rotation measures (RMs) offer a direct probe of magnetic fields, it weights magnetic fields by the free-electron density. Several probes of free electrons, including fast radio burst (FRB) dispersion measures (DMs) and kinematic SZ (kSZ) effect, are now maturing into precision tools. We combine RM$^2$ stacks from SPICE-RACS around DESI galaxy groups and ROSAT clusters with optical depth profiles constrained jointly by the FRB DM-redshift relation and the kSZ effect, and obtain 95% upper limits on the rms line-of-sight magnetic field of $<3.9$-$11.6~μ$G ($<2.3$-$6.4~μ$G) in groups (clusters) for a 10~kpc coherence length. Combining these with thermal pressure profiles inferred from tSZ-shear cross-correlations, we obtain 95% lower limits on the plasma $β$ of $>0.31$ ($>11$) in groups (clusters). Although current constraints are only limits, we forecast a first detection with larger datasets from the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA). We present the first forecast of the DSA RM grid density ($\sim365$ RMs deg$^{-2}$), which when combined with 10$^4$ FRBs would measure the field in groups to $3$-$13\%$ precision, compared to current constraints of $38$-$75\%$. Although the interpretation of current measurements remains challenging owing to depolarization along turbulent halo sightlines and the unknown coherence length, larger samples and DSA/Square Kilometer Array observations may resolve these uncertainties by measuring polarization-fraction profiles and the RM structure function using extended radio sources, respectively.

paper.title: Improving cosmological distance measurements at high redshift using Lyman-Alpha forest BAO reconstruction
paper.abstract: The Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) measures baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) in the Lyman-$α$ (Lyman-alpha) forest and provides a robust probe of the expansion history in the matter-dominated era. Yet, non-linear structure formation broadens and shifts the BAO peak. To undo these effects, we extend standard Zel'dovich reconstruction, routinely applied to galaxy surveys, to the Lyman-alpha forest. We validate our methodology on large-volume idealized Lyman-alpha forest mocks painted on top of the \textsc{AbacusSummit} $N$-body simulations, using linear control variates to suppress sample variance and thereby reduce the error bars by a factor of up to $\approx \sqrt{50}$. In fully sampled periodic boxes, reconstruction halves the radial BAO damping scale and reduces the uncertainties on the radial ($\apar$) and transverse ($\aperp$) scaling parameters by $\approx25\%$ and $\approx15\%$, respectively. It also reduces the non-linear shift from $Δ\apar=+0.3\%$ to $+0.10\pm0.07\%$, while $\aperp$ remains unbiased. To make this approach readily applicable to observational data, we demonstrate the impact of a survey mask with a DESI-like density of $50\,\mathrm{deg}^{-2}$. For this mask, we compare two approaches to estimate the displacement field: either directly from the Lyman-alpha forest or using an external tracer with a number density of $\bar n \simeq 10^{-3}\,h^3\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, such as Lyman-break galaxies and Lyman-$α$ emitters---both key targets for DESI-II. Both approaches give comparable gains and reduce the uncertainties on $\apar$ and $\aperp$ by $\approx 27\%$ and $\approx 10\%$, respectively, with mild improvements for futuristic high-density surveys with $160\,\mathrm{deg}^{-2}$. Correspondingly, the figure of merit improves by factors of $1.66$ for fully sampled boxes, $1.65$ for a DESI-like, and $1.76$ for a high-density survey.
